findings.title: Feature-gated table widgets discard the query result
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and an empty `tableData` object instead of the current `result.data`, `result.meta`, and derived fields. Consequently every dashboard table widget for an enabled organization renders with no columns and no rows, even though its query completed successfully. Pass the actual table result and column configuration to the new visualization (and preserve its loading behavior) before enabling this path.

findings.title: PR-comment formatting helpers are defined on the wrong class
findings.body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` and `_truncate_title` were added to `CommitContextIntegration`, but the new callers are `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow`, which call `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` from the `PRCommentWorkflow` hierarchy. Those workflow instances do not receive methods added to the integration class, so generating a merged-PR comment raises `AttributeError` rather than posting/updating the comment. Move these helpers to `PRCommentWorkflow` (where this method also expects `_truncate_title`), or invoke them through the workflow's integration object.

findings.title: Zero-valued age and timestamp bypass the mutual-exclusion validation
findings.body: The cross-field checks use `self.initial_data.get(...)`, which treats `0` as absent. A report containing both `{"age": 0, "timestamp": 0}` passes both validators even though both timing fields are present and timestamp explicitly permits zero. This makes the collector accept a format that its validation is intended to reject; test key presence (or perform this in serializer-level `validate`) rather than truthiness.

findings.title: Attribute-key query cache key is not scoped to the organization
findings.body: The new React Query key contains only the item type, attribute type, date range, and project IDs; unlike the previous API-query key, it omits the organization slug. With no projects selected (the common all-projects state), two organizations using the same range produce the same cache key. On an organization switch the hook can render the prior organization's cached custom attribute names, and can retain them if the refetch fails. Include `organization.slug` in the key so cached `TagCollection` data cannot bleed between organizations.
